thread:
noah: Kicking off bring-up for zephyrus-v1 embeddings in staging. Need quick recall@1/5/10 and cluster sanity.

anya: I'll run recall on the wiki and bookstore holdouts. Baseline for comparison?

lee: Use concord-v3-fp16 as baseline. I ran a small sweep: concord R@1=0.65, zephyrus R@1=0.61 on wiki (fp16).

noah: 4% gap at R@1, that's larger than expected. Any config diffs in pooling/tokenizer?

cheng: Model diff: zephyrus changed final pooling (mean->weighted mean) and we also applied a tiny label smoothing during finetune. Could affect norms.

anya: Can we check embedding L2 norms and pairwise cosine shifts? I suspect norm contraction.

lee: quick numbers from 5k sample: concord mean_norm=11.5, zephyrus-fp16 mean_norm=8.7. cosine mean shift (concord->zephyrus) = -0.03 median.

noah: that's big. Try post-hoc L2 re-scaling to baseline mean and re-run recall. If that recovers most of R@1, training config needs fix.

anya: scaled embeddings (scale=11.5/8.7) -> zephyrus R@1 jumps to 0.63 on wiki, R@5 0.83. Close but still slightly behind.

cheng: also try per-channel int8 quantization (we usually see less norm impact). ops-bot: Starting quant job: model=zephyrus-v1 quant=int8-perchannel env=staging (job id 7782).

ops-bot: Job 7782: finished, artifacts at gs://redwood-staging/zephyrus-v1/int8-perchannel/metrics.json

lee: int8-perchannel raw -> R@1=0.58, mean_norm=8.1. After rescale to 11.5 -> R@1=0.61. So quant adds some drop beyond norm shrink.

anya: What's silhouette and cluster compactness? I ran kmeans n_clusters=150 on a 20k sample. zephyrus-fp16 silhouette=0.10, concord silhouette=0.16. UMAP shows more overlap.

noah: weighted pooling change likely causing semantic mixing. Quick A/B: run zephyrus with mean pooling saved checkpoint? Can we swap pooling at inference time?

cheng: yes, checkpoint supports both pooling flags. Running fp16 mean-pool inference now.

lee: mean-pool zephyrus (fp16) -> R@1=0.64, silhouette=0.15. Nice. That pins the regression to pooling change.

noah: perfect repro. Action: ask training to produce variant with original pooling or retrain loss to preserve norms. For release, we can either use mean-pool inference flag or apply scale+pooling fallback. Which is least risky?

anya: using mean-pool inference flag for now seems safest. Also add a post-index normalization step (L2) and scaling to concord mean before serving to mitigate quantization effects.

cheng: I'll coordinate with training to rerun finetune with previous pooling and remove label smoothing for a debug epoch to see effect.

ops-bot: Deploy request: model=zephyrus-v1 pool=mean quant=fp16 env=staging -> started (job 7783).

lee: I also checked MRR and precision@1: recovered to within 0.01 of baseline after mean-pool. Good.

noah: Thanks team. Notes: 1) Pooling change caused cluster collapse/norm shift 2) Per-channel int8 helps vs symmetric but still needs scaling 3) Short-term: enable mean-pool flag for inference + L2-scale; Long-term: retrain with prior pooling.

anya: I've uploaded eval scripts, result sheets, and UMAPs to the staging bucket: gs://redwood-staging/zephyrus-v1/analysis/

noah: Closing loop: I'll open a training ticket with linking metrics and ask for a debug checkpoint. Leaving thread open for final training response. :white_check_mark:
